input.rationale: Prevent a misreading of the pre-save readiness release. processReadyToRead does not complete a read when it runs: it passes the signals to pendingReadIndex.addReady and then applies LastApplied, and pendingReadIndex.applied completes a batch only when the applied index reaches its ready index. The entry is corrected to state that completion condition, so the early release is described as recording a ready index rather than completing a read. The vote-durability conclusion is unaffected because that release carries no election state.

knowledge.statement: engine.processSteps takes one update per active node, calls applySnapshotAndUpdate, then for each update sends the free-order messages (Replicate and Ping) and calls processReadyToRead, processDroppedEntries and processDroppedReadIndexes, and only after that calls logdb.SaveRaftState for the whole batch. The remaining messages, including vote responses and read-index replies, are released by node.processRaftUpdate after the save. processReadyToRead passes its signals to pendingReadIndex.addReady and then applies LastApplied, and a batch completes only when the applied index reaches its ready index, so the pre-save release records a ready index without completing a read.
knowledge.conditions: The updates come from the engine's batch loop, each node includes its changed raft state, and the log DB implements SaveRaftState as one atomically committed write batch.
knowledge.changed_premise: The earlier statement recorded only that readiness signals reach the node layer before the batch is persisted. It now also records that processReadyToRead completes a batch only when LastApplied reaches the ready index, so the early release does not complete a read before the entries are applied.

investigations.question: When the leader confirms a later queued ReadIndex context before an earlier follower's context, does each follower receive a reply tagged with the SystemCtx it admitted, and can its pending read complete?
investigations.hypothesis: The leader batches earlier queued requests into the later confirmation but emits every remote reply with the later confirmation context. The earlier follower's pendingReadIndex therefore cannot associate the reply and leaves its batch at index zero until the client deadline expires.
investigations.discriminator: The retained execution's readindex_reply context and read_completion_state for the earlier request. A later source path or delivery rule that re-tags the reply by request identity, or completes the original batch despite the mismatched key, would change the judgment.

knowledge.assertion: The confirming context returns earlier queued requests while preserving each request's own SystemCtx.
Remote replies are tagged with the confirming heartbeat context instead of the queued request's context.
A response with a nonmatching SystemCtx leaves the original pending batch at index zero and cannot complete it.
The exercised later-confirmation ordering produced a mismatched reply context and left the earlier read batch unready after the ready index was applied.
The sequential-confirmation control completed when the admitted context was confirmed first.
The logical-deadline case returned RequestTimeout at tick 51 and removed the stale batch.
Observer-originated ReadIndex requests enter the same leader queue and pending-read response path, measured at both the leader-side reply and the observer's own consumer.
The observer leader-side reply carried the later confirming context rather than the observer's admitted context.
The observer's admitted read stayed at index zero and did not complete under the later-first ordering, while the control confirming its own context first completed with batch index 4.
A periodic heartbeat carries the newest queued context, so its first confirmation returns every earlier queued request under that context.

The tick-driven case produced a heartbeat carrying the newest context, and the earlier requester's reply carried that context while its batch stayed at index zero, whereas the single-read tick control completed.

Under one confirmation the local requester's ready-to-read result carried its own context and completed, while the earlier remote requester's reply carried the local context and its batch stayed at index zero.

investigations.question: After a leadership change, can a leader accept and commit a configuration change while an inherited configuration change is committed but not yet applied, so the newer change is committed with the pre-change quorum?
investigations.hypothesis: The pending-change gate counts only entries after the committed index and is a single boolean cleared by any applied change, so a leader that inherits a committed-but-unapplied configuration change could accept a second change and commit it with the membership that still excludes the first change.

knowledge.assertion: A leader keeps refusing further configuration-change proposals until a configuration change is applied or the peer changes term or role.

knowledge.statement: readIndex.confirm(ctx, from, quorum) confirms every queued request up to and including ctx and returns each queued readStatus with its original SystemCtx, while rewriting each returned index to the confirmed request's committed index and deleting all returned entries from the queue.
knowledge.conditions: The leader has multiple pending ReadIndex requests, ctx names a later queued request, and quorum confirmations are received for ctx.

knowledge.statement: handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation adds a local ready-to-read result with each readStatus's own ctx, but for a remote s.from it emits ReadIndexResp using the confirming heartbeat's Hint and HintHigh instead of s.ctx.
knowledge.conditions: readIndex.confirm returns at least one remote readStatus whose ctx differs from the confirming heartbeat's context.

knowledge.statement: The node registers a pending read batch under a generated SystemCtx. pendingReadIndex.addReady updates only a batch whose map key equals the response SystemCtx, and pendingReadIndex.applied completes only a batch with a nonzero ready index not exceeding the applied index. An unmatched response leaves the original batch at index zero.
knowledge.conditions: A follower-originated read is registered before a response is processed, and the response SystemCtx differs from the registered key.

knowledge.statement: In the exercised three-voter group, when two follower-originated ReadIndex requests with distinct SystemCtx values were queued and the later context was confirmed first, node 2 received a ReadIndex reply carrying node 3's context. Node 2's original admitted batch still existed at index zero after the real ReadyToRead index 4 was applied, and the later context-101 confirmation produced no context-correct reply.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 leader; node 2 and node 3 follower-originated ReadIndex requests with distinct contexts; the later context's heartbeat was delivered to node 3 and its confirmation returned to the leader before the earlier heartbeat reached node 2; the test-only in-memory ILogDB and controlled logical delivery order were used; production code was unchanged.

knowledge.statement: Under the captured legal membership and raft paths, a node that is a current voter cannot become an observer or witness while retaining its voter role: adding a current address as observer or witness is rejected, removal deletes the node from every role map and marks it removed, re-adding a removed ID is rejected, and restoring a snapshot panics if a full member appears in the observer or witness set. The leader also sends heartbeats with a nonzero ReadIndex context only to voting members. Therefore an observer cannot normally receive a voter-issued nonzero ReadIndex context through a legal transition and then confirm it as quorum support.
knowledge.conditions: The user-facing configuration-change and raft snapshot paths are used as captured; no direct mutation of internal role maps, operator role misconfiguration, forged messages, or a custom transport that changes response admission is included.

knowledge.statement: In the same three-peer in-process harness, when node 2's admitted ReadIndex context was confirmed first, the leader's reply carried that same context, the real follower handler's ReadyToRead was consumed by pendingReadIndex, whose batch index became 4, and the admitted client read completed after the ready index was applied.
knowledge.conditions: Real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; test-only in-memory ILogDB; two queued contexts; node 2's context confirmed first; node 2's reply routed through its real follower handler and pendingReadIndex consumer; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the logical-deadline case, after node 2 received the later context's reply and the real ready index was applied, the original read batch remained at index zero and did not complete before the 50-tick deadline. At logical tick 51 the pendingReadIndex GC returned RequestTimeout and removed the batch.
knowledge.conditions: Same three-peer in-process harness and later-first context ordering; a test-only in-memory ILogDB; node 2's request created with a 50-tick timeout; the applied ready index was supplied before the logical clock was advanced to 51; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: handleLeaderReadIndex rejects a witness source but does not reject an observer source; it queues the request in the same readIndex path and broadcasts the confirmation heartbeat to voting members. An observer's local ReadIndex is forwarded by handleObserverReadIndex to handleFollowerReadIndex, and its response is routed through handleObserverReadIndexResp to handleFollowerReadIndexResp and the same pendingReadIndex consumer.
knowledge.conditions: The observer has a known leader, and the leader has a committed entry in its current term and accepts the queued request. knowledge.statement: RequestAddNode promotes an existing observer only when the supplied AddNode address equals the observer's stored address. An invalid or empty target is rejected by requestConfigChange before a proposal; a different valid target is rejected by membership.isInvalidObserverPromotion. A matching address is accepted and removes the observer role.
knowledge.conditions: The user-facing RequestAddNode path, the default or configured target validator, and the membership state machine are used as captured. No execution is included; the behavior is established by the source and membership tests.

knowledge.statement: In the membership control, an observer at address a2 is promoted when the AddNode target is a2. Targets a3 and empty are rejected, and the observer role remains after both rejections.

knowledge.statement: In the observer-endpoint execution, observer 4 forwarded its own ReadIndex context to the real leader, voter 3's later context was confirmed first, and the reply addressed to observer 4 carried voter 3's context with log index 4. The observer's real handler produced a ReadyToRead carrying that later context at index 4, while the batch keyed by the observer's own context stayed at index zero and the client read did not complete. In the control, confirming the observer's own context first produced a reply carrying that context and the read completed with batch index 4.

knowledge.statement: handleLeaderPropose inspects every proposed entry, reports a configuration-change entry as dropped and replaces it with an empty application entry when pendingConfigChange is already set, and sets that flag for each configuration-change entry it inspects before appending the remaining entries and replicating them. The apply paths addNode, addObserver, addWitness and removeNode clear the flag, and reset clears it on a term or role transition, so a leader that proposed a configuration change keeps refusing new configuration changes until a configuration change is applied or the peer changes term or role.
knowledge.conditions: The peer is leader, configuration-change proposals arrive through handleLeaderPropose, and configuration changes are applied through the raft apply paths and reported by the surrounding node.

knowledge.statement: handleNodeElection refuses to campaign when log.committed exceeds the applied index, using the general committed-versus-applied check rather than a configuration-specific one, so a node with any committed but unapplied entry cannot start an election. preLeaderPromotionHandleConfigChange then counts only configuration-change entries after the committed index and re-sets the pending flag when exactly one exists, or panics when more than one exists. handleFollowerTimeoutNow reaches the same election handler because it only advances the election tick and lets the normal tick emit the Election message, and tryCommit evaluates the cluster quorum from the raft membership maps that the apply paths maintain.
knowledge.conditions: Elections start through the Election message, including the path taken after a leader-transfer TimeoutNow, and the applied index is the value the surrounding node reports after its state machine applies entries.

knowledge.statement: engine.processSteps collects one update per active node, then sends only the messages node.sendReplicateMessages admits, which isFreeOrderMessage restricts to Replicate and Ping, before calling logdb.SaveRaftState for the whole update batch. SaveRaftState writes each non-empty raft state, the entries and snapshot metadata into one write batch that the log DB commits atomically, and only after that does processSteps call node.processRaftUpdate, which appends entries to the log reader and forwards every remaining message, including RequestVoteResp, HeartbeatResp and ReadIndexResp.
knowledge.conditions: The updates are produced by the execution engine's processSteps batch loop, each peer includes its changed raft state in the update, and the log DB implements SaveRaftState as one atomically committed write batch.

knowledge.statement: NodeHost.SyncRead resolves the caller context through linearizableRead, which calls the internal readIndex helper and node.read; node.read registers the request through pendingReadIndex.read and the helper then marks the node ready, so a synchronous read waits on the same pending batch the ReadIndex protocol completes. NodeHost.ReadIndex returns the RequestState from the same helper, and ReadLocalNode refuses to read unless that state's ready-to-read flag was set. The shared result mapping returns normally on a completed result, returns ErrTimeout on a timeout result or an expired caller context, ErrClusterNotReady on a dropped result, and ErrRejected, ErrClusterClosed or ErrAborted on the other result codes.
knowledge.conditions: The caller invokes these public APIs on an initialized non-witness node, and the read batch was registered through pendingReadIndex.read before the reply is processed.

knowledge.statement: On each heartbeat timeout leaderTick emits a LeaderHeartbeat, and handleLeaderHeartbeat broadcasts a heartbeat whose context is readIndex.peepCtx when a read is pending; peepCtx returns the last queued context, which is the newest admitted request. A follower echoes that Hint and HintHigh in its HeartbeatResp, and handleLeaderHeartbeatResp passes any nonzero hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation, so a periodic heartbeat confirms the newest queued context and readIndex.confirm then returns every earlier queued request together with it.
knowledge.conditions: The node is leader with at least one pending ReadIndex request, and at least one voter responds to the periodic heartbeat carrying the newest context.

knowledge.statement: In the tick-driven execution, one leader tick with two queued follower reads produced a heartbeat carrying the newest queued context; the echo of that heartbeat confirmed it, the reply delivered to the earlier requester carried the newest context at log index 4, and that requester's admitted batch stayed at index zero after index 4 was applied, so its read did not complete. With only the earlier read queued, the same tick-driven path carried that read's own context, the reply carried the same context, and the read completed with batch index 4.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 as leader; one test-only in-memory ILogDB per node; both reads registered through the node-level pendingReadIndex and forwarded through the real follower path; a single leader Tick is the only scheduling input and the harness only chooses which follower receives that heartbeat; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the shared-confirmation execution, one leader broadcast carrying the later local context confirmed an earlier remote read from node 2 and a later leader-local read. The local requester's ready-to-read result carried its own context at index 4 and its read completed, while the reply addressed to node 2 carried the local context at index 4 and node 2's admitted batch stayed at index zero, so its read did not complete.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 as leader; the remote read registered on node 2 and forwarded through the real follower path, the local read issued on the leader; one test-only in-memory ILogDB per node; the harness delivers only the heartbeat addressed to node 3; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the multi-requester execution, three remote reads were queued in the order read-A from node 2, read-B from node 3 and read-C from node 2; one leader tick made the heartbeat carry read-C's context, the replies addressed to node 2 carried that context for both read-A and read-C, and the reply addressed to node 3 carried it for read-B. After the confirmed index 4 was applied, read-A and read-B stayed at index zero and did not complete, while read-C completed.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 as leader; one test-only in-memory ILogDB per node; all three reads registered through the node-level pendingReadIndex and forwarded through the real follower path in that order; a single leader Tick is the only scheduling input and the harness delivers only the heartbeat addressed to node 3; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: raft.restore rejects a snapshot whose index does not exceed the committed index, panics when the local node would become an observer or witness, and otherwise lets the log replace its state and set the committed and processed positions to the snapshot index. restoreRemotes then recreates the remotes, observers and witnesses maps from the snapshot membership, promoting a local observer to follower when the snapshot lists it as a full member, panicking on a witness promotion, and stepping a leader down when the snapshot no longer contains it. A running node reaches restoreRemotes through the state machine's Recover task, which the node schedules from pushSnapshot after applying the snapshot to its logs.
knowledge.conditions: A node receives or recovers from a snapshot whose index exceeds its committed index, and the node's surrounding state machine runs the scheduled Recover task.

knowledge.statement: In the admission execution, a leader for voters {1,2,3} had one ReadIndex request queued under context {101,1002}. A HeartbeatResp carrying that context from node 4, which is in no role map, left the pending queue at its previous length and produced no replies both when delivered through the Peer admission path and when handed directly to the raft state machine; the same response from voter 3 then emptied the queue and produced one ReadIndex reply addressed to the requesting node.
knowledge.conditions: A real raft state machine built by the package test helper with committed membership {1,2,3} and a committed current-term no-op; node 4 absent from remotes, observers and witnesses; the response carries the queued context in Hint and HintHigh with a zero term; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the live-removal execution, voters 1 and 2 applied a RemoveNode config change for node 3 and the voter set became {1,2}. A ReadIndex request from node 2 was then queued at the leader; a confirming HeartbeatResp from removed node 3 produced no ReadIndex reply for node 2, while the same response from current voter 2 produced exactly one reply.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 as leader; the removal applied through Peer.ApplyConfigChange on nodes 1 and 2; the read context {303,3003} forwarded by node 2; responses delivered through the real Peer admission path with a zero term; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the proposal-gate execution, a leader for voters {1,2,3} saved an AddNode for node 4 with key 9001 as one configuration-change entry and reported nothing dropped. Before that change was committed or applied, an AddNode for node 5 with key 9002 was saved as one plain application entry with no configuration-change entry, and the update reported exactly one dropped entry keyed 9002.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 as leader with a committed current-term no-op; both changes submitted through Peer.ProposeConfigChange with no follower acknowledgement delivered; the leader update inspected directly for saved entry types and dropped entries; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the retained follower snapshot-delivery execution, node 2 had committed index 4 when an InstallSnapshot at index 3 arrived; the follower exposed no snapshot and its committed index stayed 4. A following InstallSnapshot at index 10 was exposed at index 10 and advanced the follower's committed index to 10.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 as leader with a committed current-term no-op at index 4; node 2 received InstallSnapshot messages with index 3 term 1 and index 10 term 2, each carrying the current {1,2,3} membership, through its real handler; one test-only in-memory ILogDB per node; the follower's committed index was sampled from the update state reported by each pump; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: When a ReadIndex request is pending, broadcastHeartbeatMessage uses readIndex.peepCtx as the heartbeat context and broadcastHeartbeatMessageWithHint sends that hint-carrying heartbeat to every member of votingMembers(), which is the union of remotes and witnesses; observers are sent a heartbeat only when the context is zero. numVotingMembers() is len(remotes)+len(witnesses), and both quorum() and the commit path use it, so a witness acknowledgement counts toward the read quorum and the commit quorum alike. On the leader, a HeartbeatResp is admitted through lw, which resolves the sender against the current remotes, observers and witnesses maps and drops the message when it is in none of them; handleLeaderHeartbeatResp then passes a nonzero hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation, and readIndex.confirm performs no further role check.
knowledge.conditions: The node is leader with at least one pending ReadIndex request, the role maps reflect the current configuration, and a heartbeat response arrives from a node that is currently a voter, an observer, a witness, or in no role map.

history.statement: When a ReadIndex request is pending, broadcastHeartbeatMessage uses readIndex.peepCtx as the heartbeat context and broadcastHeartbeatMessageWithHint sends that hint-carrying heartbeat only to current voting members; observers receive a heartbeat only when the context is zero, and witnesses are not addressed. On the leader, a HeartbeatResp is admitted through lw, which resolves the sender against the current remotes, observers and witnesses maps and drops the message when it is in none of them, after which handleLeaderHeartbeatResp passes a nonzero hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation and readIndex.confirm counts the admitted sender without a further role check.
history.conditions: The node is leader with at least one pending ReadIndex request, the role maps reflect the current configuration, and a heartbeat response arrives from a node that is currently a voter, an observer, a witness, or in no role map.
history.correction: The earlier statement said witnesses are not addressed by the hint-carrying heartbeat and that the send-side filter excluded them from the acknowledgement count. votingMembers() includes witnesses, so they receive the hint and their acknowledgements count in both the read and commit quorums; the only sender kept from echoing a nonzero hint is an observer, which receives a heartbeat only with a zero context, and a sender outside every role map is dropped by the admission lookup.

knowledge.statement: NodeHost.SyncRead calls nh.linearizableRead with a Lookup callback. linearizableRead takes the timeout from the caller context, calls nh.readIndex, and that helper calls node.read with nh.getTimeoutTick(timeout) before marking the engine step ready. node.read rejects an uninitialized node with ErrClusterNotReady and a witness with ErrInvalidOperation, and otherwise registers the request through pendingReadIndexes.read. linearizableRead then waits on getRequestState(ctx, rs), releases the request state and runs the callback. NodeHost.ReadIndex resolves the same nh.readIndex helper and returns its RequestState to the caller.
knowledge.conditions: The caller invokes SyncRead or ReadIndex on an initialized cluster with a context that carries a deadline, and production code is unchanged.

knowledge.statement: NodeHostConfig.GetTargetValidator returns id.IsNodeHostID when AddressByNodeHostID is set, the transport factory's Validate when a TransportFactory is configured, and stringutil.IsValidAddress otherwise. node.requestConfigChange calls that predicate for every change whose type is not RemoveNode and returns ErrInvalidAddress when it fails, before constructing the ConfigChange that the membership state machine later validates.
knowledge.conditions: RequestAddNode or another non-remove membership request is issued on an initialized non-witness node, and the target is judged by the configured validator rather than by existing membership.

knowledge.statement: raft.reset replaces r.readIndex with a fresh readIndex, clears the vote and votes map, clears the pending configuration-change flag, aborts any leader transfer and rebuilds the remote, observer and witness maps. becomeCandidate, becomeLeader and the follower transition all call reset, so a pending ReadIndex request is dropped by any role transition, and a HeartbeatResp carrying its context in a later term cannot confirm it.
knowledge.conditions: The node performs a raft role transition through becomeFollower, becomeCandidate or becomeLeader while a ReadIndex request is pending.

knowledge.statement: The captured operational documentation describes adding an observer and later promoting it to a regular node while removing a failed node, and it states no requirement on the RequestAddNode target. The exported RequestAddNode comment is the only captured statement that the target is ignored when promoting an existing observer.
knowledge.conditions: The captured tree is the source of documentation; no external documentation, changelog or issue tracker is consulted.

knowledge.statement: raft.restore rejects a snapshot whose index does not exceed the committed index, panics if the local node would become an observer or witness, and then, when the local log already matches the snapshot index and term, calls commitTo on that index and returns false without invoking log.restore or restoreRemotes. Otherwise it restores the log and returns true, and restoreRemotes later rebuilds the remote, observer and witness maps from the snapshot membership.
knowledge.conditions: A node receives or recovers from a snapshot whose index exceeds its committed index, and the local log either already matches the snapshot index and term or does not.

knowledge.statement: engine.processSteps takes one update per active node, calls applySnapshotAndUpdate, then for each update sends the free-order messages (Replicate and Ping) and calls processReadyToRead, processDroppedEntries and processDroppedReadIndexes, and only after that calls logdb.SaveRaftState for the whole batch. The remaining messages, including vote responses and read-index replies, are released by node.processRaftUpdate after the save. Readiness signals therefore reach the node layer before the batch is persisted, while election-relevant responses do not.
knowledge.conditions: The updates come from the engine's batch loop, each node includes its changed raft state, and the log DB implements SaveRaftState as one atomically committed write batch.

result.summary: Corrected the batch-ordering knowledge entry so the pre-save readiness release cannot be read as an early completion. processReadyToRead passes its signals to pendingReadIndex.addReady and then applies LastApplied, and a batch completes only when the applied index reaches its ready index; the entry now states that condition, cites the existing process-ready excerpt alongside the batch-loop sources, and records the premise change with the vote-durability interpretation as its affected use. The vote-durability conclusion is unaffected because the early release carries no election state. Validation reports valid, no_change false, execution_requested false, with a knowledge update and the derived investigation effect. No execution was run.

investigations.question: When the leader confirms a later queued ReadIndex context before an earlier follower's context, does each follower receive a reply tagged with the SystemCtx it admitted, and can its pending read complete?
investigations.hypothesis: The leader batches earlier queued requests into the later confirmation but emits every remote reply with the later confirmation context. The earlier follower's pendingReadIndex therefore cannot associate the reply and leaves its batch at index zero until the client deadline expires.
investigations.discriminator: The retained execution's readindex_reply context and read_completion_state for the earlier request. A later source path or delivery rule that re-tags the reply by request identity, or completes the original batch despite the mismatched key, would change the judgment.

knowledge.assertion: The confirming context returns earlier queued requests while preserving each request's own SystemCtx.
Remote replies are tagged with the confirming heartbeat context instead of the queued request's context.
A response with a nonmatching SystemCtx leaves the original pending batch at index zero and cannot complete it.
The exercised later-confirmation ordering produced a mismatched reply context and left the earlier read batch unready after the ready index was applied.
The sequential-confirmation control completed when the admitted context was confirmed first.
The logical-deadline case returned RequestTimeout at tick 51 and removed the stale batch.
Observer-originated ReadIndex requests enter the same leader queue and pending-read response path, measured at both the leader-side reply and the observer's own consumer.
The observer leader-side reply carried the later confirming context rather than the observer's admitted context.
The observer's admitted read stayed at index zero and did not complete under the later-first ordering, while the control confirming its own context first completed with batch index 4.
A periodic heartbeat carries the newest queued context, so its first confirmation returns every earlier queued request under that context.

The tick-driven case produced a heartbeat carrying the newest context, and the earlier requester's reply carried that context while its batch stayed at index zero, whereas the single-read tick control completed.

Under one confirmation the local requester's ready-to-read result carried its own context and completed, while the earlier remote requester's reply carried the local context and its batch stayed at index zero.

investigations.question: After a leadership change, can a leader accept and commit a configuration change while an inherited configuration change is committed but not yet applied, so the newer change is committed with the pre-change quorum?
investigations.hypothesis: The pending-change gate counts only entries after the committed index and is a single boolean cleared by any applied change, so a leader that inherits a committed-but-unapplied configuration change could accept a second change and commit it with the membership that still excludes the first change.

knowledge.assertion: Non-free-order messages, including RequestVoteResp and HeartbeatResp, are forwarded only after the batch's raft state has been committed atomically.
The same batch loop releases readiness signals before SaveRaftState but sends vote responses only after it, so the early-release path does not carry election state.

knowledge.statement: readIndex.confirm(ctx, from, quorum) confirms every queued request up to and including ctx and returns each queued readStatus with its original SystemCtx, while rewriting each returned index to the confirmed request's committed index and deleting all returned entries from the queue.
knowledge.conditions: The leader has multiple pending ReadIndex requests, ctx names a later queued request, and quorum confirmations are received for ctx.

knowledge.statement: handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation adds a local ready-to-read result with each readStatus's own ctx, but for a remote s.from it emits ReadIndexResp using the confirming heartbeat's Hint and HintHigh instead of s.ctx.
knowledge.conditions: readIndex.confirm returns at least one remote readStatus whose ctx differs from the confirming heartbeat's context.

knowledge.statement: The node registers a pending read batch under a generated SystemCtx. pendingReadIndex.addReady updates only a batch whose map key equals the response SystemCtx, and pendingReadIndex.applied completes only a batch with a nonzero ready index not exceeding the applied index. An unmatched response leaves the original batch at index zero.
knowledge.conditions: A follower-originated read is registered before a response is processed, and the response SystemCtx differs from the registered key.

knowledge.statement: In the exercised three-voter group, when two follower-originated ReadIndex requests with distinct SystemCtx values were queued and the later context was confirmed first, node 2 received a ReadIndex reply carrying node 3's context. Node 2's original admitted batch still existed at index zero after the real ReadyToRead index 4 was applied, and the later context-101 confirmation produced no context-correct reply.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 leader; node 2 and node 3 follower-originated ReadIndex requests with distinct contexts; the later context's heartbeat was delivered to node 3 and its confirmation returned to the leader before the earlier heartbeat reached node 2; the test-only in-memory ILogDB and controlled logical delivery order were used; production code was unchanged.

knowledge.statement: Under the captured legal membership and raft paths, a node that is a current voter cannot become an observer or witness while retaining its voter role: adding a current address as observer or witness is rejected, removal deletes the node from every role map and marks it removed, re-adding a removed ID is rejected, and restoring a snapshot panics if a full member appears in the observer or witness set. The leader also sends heartbeats with a nonzero ReadIndex context only to voting members. Therefore an observer cannot normally receive a voter-issued nonzero ReadIndex context through a legal transition and then confirm it as quorum support.
knowledge.conditions: The user-facing configuration-change and raft snapshot paths are used as captured; no direct mutation of internal role maps, operator role misconfiguration, forged messages, or a custom transport that changes response admission is included.

knowledge.statement: In the same three-peer in-process harness, when node 2's admitted ReadIndex context was confirmed first, the leader's reply carried that same context, the real follower handler's ReadyToRead was consumed by pendingReadIndex, whose batch index became 4, and the admitted client read completed after the ready index was applied.
knowledge.conditions: Real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; test-only in-memory ILogDB; two queued contexts; node 2's context confirmed first; node 2's reply routed through its real follower handler and pendingReadIndex consumer; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the logical-deadline case, after node 2 received the later context's reply and the real ready index was applied, the original read batch remained at index zero and did not complete before the 50-tick deadline. At logical tick 51 the pendingReadIndex GC returned RequestTimeout and removed the batch.
knowledge.conditions: Same three-peer in-process harness and later-first context ordering; a test-only in-memory ILogDB; node 2's request created with a 50-tick timeout; the applied ready index was supplied before the logical clock was advanced to 51; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: handleLeaderReadIndex rejects a witness source but does not reject an observer source; it queues the request in the same readIndex path and broadcasts the confirmation heartbeat to voting members. An observer's local ReadIndex is forwarded by handleObserverReadIndex to handleFollowerReadIndex, and its response is routed through handleObserverReadIndexResp to handleFollowerReadIndexResp and the same pendingReadIndex consumer.
knowledge.conditions: The observer has a known leader, and the leader has a committed entry in its current term and accepts the queued request. Two retained receipts now exercise this path: the leader-side observer receipt measures the reply the leader addresses to the observer, and the observer-endpoint receipt measures a real observer peer forwarding its own request plus its real handler and the node-level pendingReadIndex consuming the reply.

knowledge.statement: RequestAddNode promotes an existing observer only when the supplied AddNode address equals the observer's stored address. An invalid or empty target is rejected by requestConfigChange before a proposal; a different valid target is rejected by membership.isInvalidObserverPromotion. A matching address is accepted and removes the observer role.
knowledge.conditions: The user-facing RequestAddNode path, the default or configured target validator, and the membership state machine are used as captured. No execution is included; the behavior is established by the source and membership tests.

knowledge.statement: In the membership control, an observer at address a2 is promoted when the AddNode target is a2. Targets a3 and empty are rejected, and the observer role remains after both rejections.
knowledge.conditions: Internal membership state machine with OrderedConfigChange enabled; fresh membership per case; observer 100 at a2; AddNode at index 1000; test-only direct invocation, no NodeHost target validator or transport.

knowledge.statement: In the observer-endpoint execution, observer 4 forwarded its own ReadIndex context to the real leader, voter 3's later context was confirmed first, and the reply addressed to observer 4 carried voter 3's context with log index 4. The observer's real handler produced a ReadyToRead carrying that later context at index 4, while the batch keyed by the observer's own context stayed at index zero and the client read did not complete. In the control, confirming the observer's own context first produced a reply carrying that context and the read completed with batch index 4.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 as leader; node 4 recorded as an observer in each voter through Peer.ApplyConfigChange; a real observer Raft peer launched with IsObserver whose log DB carries the committed voter membership; one test-only in-memory ILogDB per node; controlled message delivery order; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: handleLeaderPropose inspects every proposed entry, reports a configuration-change entry as dropped and replaces it with an empty application entry when pendingConfigChange is already set, and sets that flag for each configuration-change entry it inspects before appending the remaining entries and replicating them. The apply paths addNode, addObserver, addWitness and removeNode clear the flag, and reset clears it on a term or role transition, so a leader that proposed a configuration change keeps refusing new configuration changes until a configuration change is applied or the peer changes term or role.
knowledge.conditions: The peer is leader, configuration-change proposals arrive through handleLeaderPropose, and configuration changes are applied through the raft apply paths and reported by the surrounding node.

knowledge.statement: handleNodeElection refuses to campaign when log.committed exceeds the applied index, using the general committed-versus-applied check rather than a configuration-specific one, so a node with any committed but unapplied entry cannot start an election. preLeaderPromotionHandleConfigChange then counts only configuration-change entries after the committed index and re-sets the pending flag when exactly one exists, or panics when more than one exists. handleFollowerTimeoutNow reaches the same election handler because it only advances the election tick and lets the normal tick emit the Election message, and tryCommit evaluates the cluster quorum from the raft membership maps that the apply paths maintain.
knowledge.conditions: Elections start through the Election message, including the path taken after a leader-transfer TimeoutNow, and the applied index is the value the surrounding node reports after its state machine applies entries.

knowledge.statement: engine.processSteps collects one update per active node, then sends only the messages node.sendReplicateMessages admits, which isFreeOrderMessage restricts to Replicate and Ping, before calling logdb.SaveRaftState for the whole update batch. SaveRaftState writes each non-empty raft state, the entries and snapshot metadata into one write batch that the log DB commits atomically, and only after that does processSteps call node.processRaftUpdate, which appends entries to the log reader and forwards every remaining message, including RequestVoteResp, HeartbeatResp and ReadIndexResp.
knowledge.conditions: The updates are produced by the execution engine's processSteps batch loop, each peer includes its changed raft state in the update, and the log DB implements SaveRaftState as one atomically committed write batch.

knowledge.statement: NodeHost.SyncRead resolves the caller context through linearizableRead, which calls the internal readIndex helper and node.read; node.read registers the request through pendingReadIndex.read and the helper then marks the node ready, so a synchronous read waits on the same pending batch the ReadIndex protocol completes. NodeHost.ReadIndex returns the RequestState from the same helper, and ReadLocalNode refuses to read unless that state's ready-to-read flag was set. The shared result mapping returns normally on a completed result, returns ErrTimeout on a timeout result or an expired caller context, ErrClusterNotReady on a dropped result, and ErrRejected, ErrClusterClosed or ErrAborted on the other result codes.
knowledge.conditions: The caller invokes these public APIs on an initialized non-witness node, and the read batch was registered through pendingReadIndex.read before the reply is processed.

knowledge.statement: On each heartbeat timeout leaderTick emits a LeaderHeartbeat, and handleLeaderHeartbeat broadcasts a heartbeat whose context is readIndex.peepCtx when a read is pending; peepCtx returns the last queued context, which is the newest admitted request. A follower echoes that Hint and HintHigh in its HeartbeatResp, and handleLeaderHeartbeatResp passes any nonzero hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation, so a periodic heartbeat confirms the newest queued context and readIndex.confirm then returns every earlier queued request together with it.
knowledge.conditions: The node is leader with at least one pending ReadIndex request, and at least one voter responds to the periodic heartbeat carrying the newest context.

knowledge.statement: In the tick-driven execution, one leader tick with two queued follower reads produced a heartbeat carrying the newest queued context; the echo of that heartbeat confirmed it, the reply delivered to the earlier requester carried the newest context at log index 4, and that requester's admitted batch stayed at index zero after index 4 was applied, so its read did not complete. With only the earlier read queued, the same tick-driven path carried that read's own context, the reply carried the same context, and the read completed with batch index 4.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 as leader; one test-only in-memory ILogDB per node; both reads registered through the node-level pendingReadIndex and forwarded through the real follower path; a single leader Tick is the only scheduling input and the harness only chooses which follower receives that heartbeat; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the shared-confirmation execution, one leader broadcast carrying the later local context confirmed an earlier remote read from node 2 and a later leader-local read. The local requester's ready-to-read result carried its own context at index 4 and its read completed, while the reply addressed to node 2 carried the local context at index 4 and node 2's admitted batch stayed at index zero, so its read did not complete.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 as leader; the remote read registered on node 2 and forwarded through the real follower path, the local read issued on the leader; one test-only in-memory ILogDB per node; the harness delivers only the heartbeat addressed to node 3; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the multi-requester execution, three remote reads were queued in the order read-A from node 2, read-B from node 3 and read-C from node 2; one leader tick made the heartbeat carry read-C's context, the replies addressed to node 2 carried that context for both read-A and read-C, and the reply addressed to node 3 carried it for read-B. After the confirmed index 4 was applied, read-A and read-B stayed at index zero and did not complete, while read-C completed.
knowledge.conditions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 as leader; one test-only in-memory ILogDB per node; all three reads registered through the node-level pendingReadIndex and forwarded through the real follower path in that order; a single leader Tick is the only scheduling input and the harness delivers only the heartbeat addressed to node 3; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: raft.restore rejects a snapshot whose index does not exceed the committed index, panics when the local node would become an observer or witness, and otherwise lets the log replace its state and set the committed and processed positions to the snapshot index. restoreRemotes then recreates the remotes, observers and witnesses maps from the snapshot membership, promoting a local observer to follower when the snapshot lists it as a full member, panicking on a witness promotion, and stepping a leader down when the snapshot no longer contains it. A running node reaches restoreRemotes through the state machine's Recover task, which the node schedules from pushSnapshot after applying the snapshot to its logs.
knowledge.conditions: A node receives or recovers from a snapshot whose index exceeds its committed index, and the node's surrounding state machine runs the scheduled Recover task.

knowledge.statement: In the admission execution, a leader for voters {1,2,3} had one ReadIndex request queued under context {101,1002}. A HeartbeatResp carrying that context from node 4, which is in no role map, left the pending queue at its previous length and produced no replies both when delivered through the Peer admission path and when handed directly to the raft state machine; the same response from voter 3 then emptied the queue and produced one ReadIndex reply addressed to the requesting node.
knowledge.conditions: A real raft state machine built by the package test helper with committed membership {1,2,3} and a committed current-term no-op; node 4 absent from remotes, observers and witnesses; the response carries the queued context in Hint and HintHigh with a zero term; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the live-removal execution, voters 1 and 2 applied a RemoveNode config change for node 3 and the voter set became {1,2}. A ReadIndex request from node 2 was then queued at the leader; a confirming HeartbeatResp from removed node 3 produced no ReadIndex reply for node 2, while the same response from current voter 2 produced exactly one reply.

knowledge.statement: When a ReadIndex request is pending, broadcastHeartbeatMessage uses readIndex.peepCtx as the heartbeat context and broadcastHeartbeatMessageWithHint sends that hint-carrying heartbeat to every member of votingMembers(), which is the union of remotes and witnesses; observers are sent a heartbeat only when the context is zero. numVotingMembers() is len(remotes)+len(witnesses), and both quorum() and the commit path use it, so a witness acknowledgement counts toward the read quorum and the commit quorum alike. On the leader, a HeartbeatResp is admitted through lw, which resolves the sender against the current remotes, observers and witnesses maps and drops the message when it is in none of them; handleLeaderHeartbeatResp then passes a nonzero hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation, and readIndex.confirm performs no further role check.
knowledge.conditions: The node is leader with at least one pending ReadIndex request, the role maps reflect the current configuration, and a heartbeat response arrives from a node that is currently a voter, an observer, a witness, or in no role map.

history.statement: When a ReadIndex request is pending, broadcastHeartbeatMessage uses readIndex.peepCtx as the heartbeat context and broadcastHeartbeatMessageWithHint sends that hint-carrying heartbeat only to current voting members; observers receive a heartbeat only when the context is zero, and witnesses are not addressed. On the leader, a HeartbeatResp is admitted through lw, which resolves the sender against the current remotes, observers and witnesses maps and drops the message when it is in none of them, after which handleLeaderHeartbeatResp passes a nonzero hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation and readIndex.confirm counts the admitted sender without a further role check.
history.conditions: The node is leader with at least one pending ReadIndex request, the role maps reflect the current configuration, and a heartbeat response arrives from a node that is currently a voter, an observer, a witness, or in no role map.
history.correction: The earlier statement said witnesses are not addressed by the hint-carrying heartbeat and that the send-side filter excluded them from the acknowledgement count. votingMembers() includes witnesses, so they receive the hint and their acknowledgements count in both the read and commit quorums; the only sender kept from echoing a nonzero hint is an observer, which receives a heartbeat only with a zero context, and a sender outside every role map is dropped by the admission lookup.

knowledge.statement: NodeHost.SyncRead calls nh.linearizableRead with a Lookup callback. linearizableRead takes the timeout from the caller context, calls nh.readIndex, and that helper calls node.read with nh.getTimeoutTick(timeout) before marking the engine step ready. node.read rejects an uninitialized node with ErrClusterNotReady and a witness with ErrInvalidOperation, and otherwise registers the request through pendingReadIndexes.read. linearizableRead then waits on getRequestState(ctx, rs), releases the request state and runs the callback. NodeHost.ReadIndex resolves the same nh.readIndex helper and returns its RequestState to the caller.
knowledge.conditions: The caller invokes SyncRead or ReadIndex on an initialized cluster with a context that carries a deadline, and production code is unchanged.

knowledge.statement: NodeHostConfig.GetTargetValidator returns id.IsNodeHostID when AddressByNodeHostID is set, the transport factory's Validate when a TransportFactory is configured, and stringutil.IsValidAddress otherwise. node.requestConfigChange calls that predicate for every change whose type is not RemoveNode and returns ErrInvalidAddress when it fails, before constructing the ConfigChange that the membership state machine later validates.
knowledge.conditions: RequestAddNode or another non-remove membership request is issued on an initialized non-witness node, and the target is judged by the configured validator rather than by existing membership.

knowledge.statement: raft.reset replaces r.readIndex with a fresh readIndex, clears the vote and votes map, clears the pending configuration-change flag, aborts any leader transfer and rebuilds the remote, observer and witness maps. becomeCandidate, becomeLeader and the follower transition all call reset, so a pending ReadIndex request is dropped by any role transition, and a HeartbeatResp carrying its context in a later term cannot confirm it.
knowledge.conditions: The node performs a raft role transition through becomeFollower, becomeCandidate or becomeLeader while a ReadIndex request is pending.

knowledge.statement: The captured operational documentation describes adding an observer and later promoting it to a regular node while removing a failed node, and it states no requirement on the RequestAddNode target. The exported RequestAddNode comment is the only captured statement that the target is ignored when promoting an existing observer.

knowledge.statement: raft.restore rejects a snapshot whose index does not exceed the committed index, panics if the local node would become an observer or witness, and then, when the local log already matches the snapshot index and term, calls commitTo on that index and returns false without invoking log.restore or restoreRemotes. Otherwise it restores the log and returns true, and restoreRemotes later rebuilds the remote, observer and witness maps from the snapshot membership.
knowledge.conditions: A node receives or recovers from a snapshot whose index exceeds its committed index, and the local log either already matches the snapshot index and term or does not.

knowledge.statement: engine.processSteps takes one update per active node, calls applySnapshotAndUpdate, then for each update sends the free-order messages (Replicate and Ping) and calls processReadyToRead, processDroppedEntries and processDroppedReadIndexes, and only after that calls logdb.SaveRaftState for the whole batch. The remaining messages, including vote responses and read-index replies, are released by node.processRaftUpdate after the save. processReadyToRead passes its signals to pendingReadIndex.addReady and then applies LastApplied, and a batch completes only when the applied index reaches its ready index, so the pre-save release records a ready index without completing a read.
knowledge.conditions: The updates come from the engine's batch loop, each node includes its changed raft state, and the log DB implements SaveRaftState as one atomically committed write batch.

history.statement: engine.processSteps takes one update per active node, calls applySnapshotAndUpdate, then for each update sends the free-order messages (Replicate and Ping) and calls processReadyToRead, processDroppedEntries and processDroppedReadIndexes, and only after that calls logdb.SaveRaftState for the whole batch. The remaining messages, including vote responses and read-index replies, are released by node.processRaftUpdate after the save. Readiness signals therefore reach the node layer before the batch is persisted, while election-relevant responses do not.
history.conditions: The updates come from the engine's batch loop, each node includes its changed raft state, and the log DB implements SaveRaftState as one atomically committed write batch.
history.correction: The earlier statement recorded only that readiness signals reach the node layer before the batch is persisted. It now also records that processReadyToRead completes a batch only when LastApplied reaches the ready index, so the early release does not complete a read before the entries are applied.
